title: Pilonidal sinus treatment studying the options: trial of pit-picking plus fibrin glue vs other minimally invasive surgeries
official: Pilonidal sinus treatment studying the options: trial of pit-picking plus fibrin glue vs other minimally invasive surgeries
summary:
Background and study aims 
Pilonidal sinus disease (PSD) is a condition that usually affects the skin just at the top of the buttocks near the tailbone. It is a chronic condition characterised by a small hole, sinus, or cyst that develops in the skin and often becomes infected. Infection will cause pain and swelling in the area and a pus-filled skin abscess can develop. 
The cure for PSD usually requires surgery, with two main surgical approaches. One involves removing the affected skin and closing the wound, the other aims to save the skin by using so-called minimally invasive surgery (MIS). The PITSTOP study concluded that the burden after surgery for PSD is high and treatment failure common. MIS may improve outcomes at the expense of a 10% higher risk of treatment failure. The most appropriate treatment depends on the type and severity of a patient’s disease, but for those patients who are suitable for MIS, there are several different techniques that can be used. 
At the moment, we do not know whether one MIS is better than the other; PITSTOP found that ‘Pit picking + glue’ is the most common MIS in the UK. In this trial we will compare this technique to other MIS procedures used as standard of care within the UK NHS. 

Who can participate? 
Patients aged 16 years and over who are undergoing MIS for PSD

What does the study involve? 
Participants will be randomly assigned to have either the pit-picking plus glue or whatever other type of operation that the surgeon thinks is best. The patient will not know which surgery they have had. After their surgery, each patient will be followed up at numerous time points, up to 1 year after surgery, to see how they are recovering.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Not provided at time of registration

Where is the study run from?
Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
September 2026 to February 2030

Who is funding the study?
National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) (UK)

Who is the main contact?
1. Prof. Steven Brown, steven.brown13@nhs.net
2. Ms Gemma Hackney, PITSTOP2@sheffield.ac.uk

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Adult patients over 16 years old 
2. Pilonidal sinus disease (including recurrent disease) where elective minimally invasive surgery (MIS) is planned
3. Able to give informed consent
4. Symptomatic pilonidal sinus disease (pain, discharge, bleeding)
Exclusion criteria:
1. Acute abscess
2. Hypersensitivity to tissue glue
3. Pregnancy (tested as per routine care)
